youtube.title: Why GTA 6 Runs at 30 FPS on Your PS5
youtube.description: If you're buying GTA 6 on console, you may want to know Rockstar hasn't committed to a 60 fps mode at launch. Rob Nelson, Rockstar North's head of development, reportedly told YouTuber Davy Jones the consoles run at 30 fps for now, and Digital Foundry thinks the CPU is the bottleneck. Red Dead 2 still has no official 60 fps upgrade, so the pattern is familiar. Sources: Kotaku, Tom's Hardware, Flow Games.

Why Rockstar Hasn't Promised GTA 6 at 60 FPS

claims.claim: Rockstar has not committed to a 60 fps option for GTA 6 on consoles at launch.
Rob Nelson, head of development at Rockstar North, reportedly told YouTuber Davy Jones the consoles are currently running the game at 30 fps.
Nelson said he would need to 'consult the technical team' about whether 60 fps comes at launch or later.
The interview was reported via Davy Jones's Flow Games podcast.
Digital Foundry theorizes that NPC density, dynamic weather, physics and traffic AI make the CPU the bottleneck rather than the GPU.
Red Dead Redemption 2 still has no official 60 fps upgrade on modern consoles.
The gameplay reveal happened about three months before launch.

issues.quote: Digital Foundry blames the CPU, not the GPU, choking on crowds, weather and traffic AI.
issues.problem: Tom's Hardware describes this as Digital Foundry 'theorizing'; 'blames' is a touch firmer than the source, though the on-screen card correctly labels it 'Digital Foundry's theory'.

check.summary: All factual claims trace to Kotaku and Tom's Hardware: Nelson's 'consult the technical team' remark via Flow Games, the 30 fps 'for now' statement, Digital Foundry's CPU-bottleneck theory, and RDR2 lacking an official 60 fps upgrade on current consoles. The script consistently hedges with 'reportedly' and on-screen text is supported. Only a slight overstatement of Digital Foundry's theory as 'blame'.
